explanation: Fires on an English preposition or infinitival 'to' that directly follows a positive evaluative, manner or ability predicate (looks good/great/nice on, works well/fast on, good at, fine/happy with, keen on, able/ready/easy/happy to), the light verbs get/got/kept (got on, got into, kept on) or 'its way'/'further' (makes its way into), and on 'only' right after a copula or auxiliary (it's only, is only, will/can only). The same prepositions stay weak (below about a quarter of max) after ordinary posture or motion verbs (sat on, fell into, jumped onto, walked into), after negative or emotional adjectives (bad at, sorry for, proud of, tired of, interested in), in fixed phrases (based on, click on) and inside noun phrases (price of); sentence-initial 'Only' is weak too.
